purpose: Menu of actions that opens at the pointer when the user right-clicks an area, presses `Shift+F10` or the context-menu key inside it, or long-presses it on touch. It is the right-click twin of `DropdownMenu`: the root `ContextMenu` owns open state, the pointer anchor, positioning and focus return through the same internal menu core, `ContextMenu.Trigger` marks the area that listens, and the item parts are DropdownMenu's own (`Group`, `Item` with its checkbox and radio kinds, `Sub`, `SubTrigger`, `SubContent`), attached to the compound so the two menus look and behave the same.
useWhen: Use ContextMenu for the same actions as a DropdownMenu, opened by right-click or long-press on an item; opened from a button use DropdownMenu.
Secondary actions on an object the user is pointing at: a table row, a file in a browser, a tree node, a canvas.
Power-user shortcuts that also exist elsewhere in the interface.
avoidWhen: The only way to reach an action. Right-click is invisible; every action in a context menu must also be reachable from a visible control (a row-actions `DropdownMenu`, a toolbar button).
A menu opened from a button → use `dropdown-menu`.
A searchable palette of commands → use `command`.
Free-form content such as forms → use `popover`.
related: dropdown-menu` — same panel, items and keyboard model, opened from a trigger button; `ContextMenu` reuses its item parts.
popover` — free-form floating content on the same `usePlacement` positioning.
table` — row actions usually pair a visible `DropdownMenu` with a `ContextMenu` around the rows.
bestPractices: Wrap the object, not the page: one `ContextMenu.Trigger` around the table body, the file grid or the tree, and read which row was targeted from your own state (for example the row the `contextmenu` came from, captured with a native `@contextmenu` on the row).
Mirror the visible row-actions menu; a context menu adds speed, never exclusive actions.
Keep it short (under about ten items), group with `ContextMenu.Group`, and put destructive actions in their own last group.
Give the panel a name with `aria-label` when the target is not obvious from focus (for example `aria-label="Actions for production"`).
disabled` gives the area back to the browser's native menu.
